sentences.text: Wpcrl/337/2024 on 16 April, 2024

Author: Rakesh Thapliyal
Bench: Rakesh Thapliyal

No  Registrar's order with  Signatures  WPCRL No. 337 of 2024  With  IA 1/2024 (For Compounding Application)
 Hon'ble Rakesh Thapliyal, J.
1.
Mr. B.S. Koranga, learned counsel for the petitioner.
2. Mr. V.K. Gemini, learned Deputy Advocate General along with Mrs. Meenakshi Sharma, learned Brief Holder for the State.
3. Mr. Arvind Kumar Verma, learned counsel for the respondents.

4. The present writ petition has been preferred along with the compounding application for quashing of the First Information Report No. 064 of 2023 dated 10.05.2023, wherein, the present petitioner has been implicated for the offence punishable under Sections 363, 366, 376 of IPC and Section 5/6 of POCSO Act, 2012, P.S. Kelakhera, District Udham Sigh Nagar.
5. The compounding application is supported with the affidavit of the petitioner as well as respondent nos. 3 and 4.
Respondent no. 3 is the father of the respondent no. 4, the victim.
The petitioner as well as respondent nos. 3 and 4 are present in court and are duly identified by their respective counsels.

6. It is contended in the compounding application that at the time of the incident the victim was 17 years and 6 months old and when she became major she now married with the petitioner on 08.01.2024 and the said marriage was also registered in the office of Registrar by the Registrar Compulsory Registration of Marriages, Bajpur, District Udham Singh Nagar and the certificate was also issued on 21.02.2024, copy of which is also annexed as Annexure-2.
WPCRL/337/2024 on 16 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/77642498/
1 7.
The respondent no. 3, the father of the victim, who is also present in court, submits that he is happy with this marriage and he does not want to proceed with this FIR.

8. This Court also interacts with the respondent and the petitioner and both of them submit that now they are married with each other and their marriage was also registered; therefore, the proceedings be dropped.

9. Learned Deputy Advocate General Mr. V.K. Gemini along with learned Brief Holder Mrs.
Meenakshi Sharma

submits before this Court that though the allegation appears to be serious in nature, but taking into consideration that the petitioner is now married with respondent no. 4 and their marriage is also registered there is no useful purpose to continue with this proceeding since it spoils the married life of the petitioner and the respondent no. 4 and if such a proceeding is permitted to continue, the same will amount to a futile exercise.
10. Finally, the State counsel submits that after taking into consideration that the petitioner married with the respondent no. 3 the offence may be compounded and the proceeding be withdrawn.

11. After taking into consideration all these aspects, particularly, the fact that the petitioner is married with respondent no. 4 and the marriage is registered and this marriage is accepted by the father of the victim, this Court is of the view that compounding application deserves to be allowed.
12. Hence, the compounding application is allowed.
The FIR No. 64 of 2023 for the offence punishable under Sections 363, 366, 376 of IPC and 5/6 of POCSO Act 2012 is quashed.

(Rakesh Thapliyal, J.) 16.04.2024 PR WPCRL/337/2024 on 16 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/77642498/
